newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends with strong gains, others recover.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends with strong gains, others recover.

text.p: Copper prices rose strongly on Wednesday, boosted by U.S.-led gains late on Tuesday and follow-through short-covering in subdued trade.
Other base metals rose in response as some confidence returned to what was recently decribed as an overwhelmingly bearish London Metal Exchange (LME).
Benchmark three month LME copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,925 a tonne, up $55 from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close and at the high of the day.
Traders were looking for more short term gains, with the next upside target pegged at $1,950.
"The market does look slightly more positive on the charts," said one broker.
"The market was short last week so we have had some covering today and we have also seen some trade buying coming in, although not in huge volumes yet," he added.

Physical traders noted a pick-up in demand for European LME copper warrants, with shipments said to be heading for the Far East and merchants more willing to rebuild stocks now that nearby backwardations have all but disappeared.
"The other factor is that copper is still relatively cheap compared to what it was four to five months ago," said a trader.
Aluminium rose with copper, gaining $13.50 to $1,433.
"The aluminium market was well oversold and due for a bounce," said one trader.
But the downside risk remained as long as LME stocks continued to mount at good rates, dealers said.
Zinc rose in the wake of the firmer overall trend, adding $16 to $1,041. Sizeable falls in stocks were lending background support, although Wednesday's rally was more short-covering, traders said.
Lead gained $16 to $788, paring some of the recent heavy losses.
On the charts lead closed back above an important rising trendline below which prices slumped during Tuesday's sell-off.
The first upside target was pegged at the psychological $800 barrier.

Tin rose $70 to $6,140 and also managed to close back above trendline support. Resistance was expected to emerge just below $6,200 based on a small chart gap and a cluster of short term moving averages.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,245/50 from $1,235.
